clue.text: Her protest was in the altogether unusual form of a very giddy 'olá'!

definitions.text: Her protest was in the altogether

indicators.note: an unusual form of some words is those words rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the Portuguese greeting, its letters taken as written without the accent

explanation.surface: A naked protester is pictured greeting the crowd with a dizzy Iberian hello.
explanation.walkthrough: The legendary Lady Godiva rode naked through Coventry to protest her husband's taxes; 'in the altogether' means naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says the countess rode naked through Coventry in protest at heavy taxes, so her protest was made nude.

clue.text: Instrument that's lifted things out of one's mouth

indicators.note: words coming out of one's mouth are spoken aloud, so the sound matters

parts.note: lifted means stolen, and stolen goods are loot

explanation.surface: An instrument that has stolen things from someone's mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Some pronounce the instrument with a y-sound, but in the common pronunciation it matches the word for stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: The lute is a plucked stringed instrument with a pear-shaped body, popular in Renaissance music.

clue.text: Provide somewhere to retire in Split

definitions.meaning: read literally, to supply someone with a bed to go to sleep in
to split is slang for to leave quickly, to run off

explanation.surface: Provide a bed for someone in a split-up home.
explanation.walkthrough: Do a bunk is British slang for running away, often to avoid paying.
explanation.definitionFit: Do a bunk is British slang meaning to flee or abscond, matching split in the sense of leave.

clue.text: Shot a young British man at a location in the Caribbean

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A news report about a young Briton shot dead on a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as gunfire but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Guantanamo Bay is an inlet on the south-east coast of Cuba, home to a US naval base and detention camp.

clue.text: Governess expected girl to turn up

parts.note: due means expected, as in the train is due

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A governess is due, and a girl is waiting for her to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman acting as chaperone and governess to girls in a Spanish family.

clue.text: See Parisian to the lobby, making for London station

parts.note: V is short for vide, Latin for see
aux is French for to the, before a plural
a hall is an entrance lobby

explanation.surface: Show a Parisian visitor to the hotel lobby, then head for a London station.
explanation.walkthrough: Vauxhall is a railway and Underground station in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Vauxhall is a main-line rail and Tube station south of the River Thames in London.

clue.text: Brandy is stuff for knocking back!

indicators.note: knocking a word back means reading it in the reverse direction

parts.note: to stuff is to cram, as with food

explanation.surface: A drinker praises brandy as the ideal thing for downing in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' looks like drinking, which suits brandy, but it signals the reversal of CRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a French brandy distilled from grape pressings left after winemaking.

clue.text: Beneath the chaos of Smithfield, a cook finds fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece goes beneath the first
Smithfield is a London meat market where cockney speech drops the h

parts.note: havoc is chaos and disorder
to do food is to cook it, as in do the potatoes

explanation.surface: In the bustle of a London meat market, a cook comes across some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Smithfield is London's old meat market, and cockney speech there drops the H of HAVOC. In a down clue A DO goes beneath 'AVOC.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is a pear-shaped fruit with green buttery flesh around a large stone.

clue.text: Light work sends one manager into a deep sleep!

indicators.note: one piece sent into another is placed inside it

parts.note: a coma is a state of deep unconsciousness
I is the Roman numeral for one
a coper is one who copes, a manager

explanation.surface: A lightweight task sends a manager into a deep sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light work' reads as an easy task but means a light-hearted stage work.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic opera is a genre of light, humorous opera with spoken dialogue, such as operetta.

clue.text: Buttery snack a head briefly comes in to consume

indicators.note: one piece coming in to another is placed inside it

parts.note: to take food or drink is to consume it

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a head, as in a price per head, means each

explanation.surface: Someone describes a buttered snack that a visitor drops in to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' cuts EACH to EAC, which 'comes in' to TAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a light sweet bun, usually toasted and served with butter at teatime.

clue.text: College class gets even

parts.note: uni is the informal short form of university, a college
a form is a class in a British school

explanation.surface: A college whose classes all end up level.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform means consistent and unvarying, the same as even in the sense of regular.

clue.text: Stamp one's feet when denied payment for entertainer

parts.note: an impression is a mark stamped onto something
I for one, plus S, as one is

indicators.note: being denied something means it is removed from the word

parts.note: a fee is a payment

explanation.surface: An entertainer stamps their feet when refused their fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when denied' takes FEE from FEET, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: An impressionist is a performer who mimics the voices and mannerisms of famous people for entertainment.

clue.text: Meat from dog leg quickly halved

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

indicators.note: halved means only one half of the doubled word is kept

parts.note: chop-chop is an informal command meaning quickly

explanation.surface: A butcher's cut taken from a dog's leg in a hurried half-chop.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is the on side, hence ON; 'halved' keeps CHOP from chop-chop.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutton chop is a cut of meat taken from a sheep's rib or loin.

clue.text: Familiar complaint covering section of Circle Line

indicators.note: the two clue words cover the answer, holding it inside their letters

explanation.surface: A commuter grumbles, as usual, about one stretch of the London Underground's Circle line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle line is a London Underground route; the answer sits inside familiAR Complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a curved stretch of a circle's circumference, a portion of that curved line.

clue.text: No doubt hollow breeze blocks not properly secured?

indicators.note: a piece that blocks another stands in its way, inside it

parts.note: ill means badly or not properly
bound means tied up, secured

indicators.note: hollow means the inside letters of the word are removed

explanation.surface: Breeze blocks with hollow cores have not been fixed properly.
explanation.walkthrough: Breeze blocks are building blocks made with cinders; 'hollow' leaves only B and E of 'breeze'.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an old-fashioned way of saying you are certain, without doubt.

clue.text: Taste heavy defeat having got caught out

indicators.note: having got something out means it is removed from the word

parts.note: a licking is a thrashing, a heavy defeat
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A team develops a taste for losing badly after a batsman is dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: A liking is a taste or fondness for something, as in a taste for jazz.

clue.text: A shout backing ring performance

indicators.note: backing means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a yell is a loud shout
O looks like a ring
op, short for opus, is a musical work or performance

explanation.surface: A cry of support for a circus ring act.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the cry is the one called out to cheer on an acrobatic act in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Alley-oop is an exclamation called out to encourage a leap or acrobatic trick, as in a circus act.

clue.text: Dance I don't like that young lady loves

parts.note: boo is an exclamation of disapproval
gal is an informal word for a girl
love is nil in tennis, written O, so two of them make OO

explanation.surface: A dance a girl adores, though the speaker disapproves.
explanation.definitionFit: The boogaloo is a dance to rock and roll or soul music, popular in the 1960s.

clue.text: X certificate show one's behind is rare event

parts.note: an X certificate marked an adult film, and blue means pornographic
to moon is to bare one's buttocks

explanation.surface: Showing an adult film and baring your bottom is a rare occurrence.
explanation.walkthrough: The old British X certificate marked films for adults only.
explanation.definitionFit: Once in a blue moon is an idiom for very rarely, so the phrase names an infrequent occurrence.

clue.text: Kitty's heading off: it follows bear

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, here taken off

parts.note: a kitty is a pool or fund of money
ergo is Latin for therefore, meaning it follows

explanation.surface: A cat sets off ahead, with a bear trailing behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' looks like a cat but is a shared pool of money.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to endure or suffer it, and undergo means the same.

clue.text: Line in front causes obstruction: none must enter

indicators.note: one piece entering another is placed inside it

parts.note: something that causes obstruction is a bar to progress
O, the figure nought, stands for none

explanation.surface: Someone standing at the front of a queue blocks it and lets nobody pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' and 'in front' suggest a queue, but this is weather: isobars are drawn on maps alongside weather fronts.
explanation.definitionFit: Isobars are lines joining points of equal pressure on a weather chart, drawn around the fronts.

clue.text: Hairstyle that has combs removed from it

definitions.text: Hairstyle that has combs removed from it

parts.words: Hairstyle that has combs removed from it
parts.note: combs suggest grooming, but a hive has honeycombs taken out of it by the keeper

explanation.surface: A hairdo from which hair combs have been pulled out.
explanation.walkthrough: A hairstyle could have combs taken out, but so does a bees' home when honey is collected.
explanation.definitionFit: The bouffant hairstyle is named for its domed shape, like a bees' nest of straw.

clue.text: No sign of hesitation for the present, or the future?

indicators.note: no means the hesitation is absent, taken out of the word

parts.note: an offering is a present or gift
er is the sound a speaker makes when hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone without hesitation hands over a gift for now, or perhaps later.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because 'in the offing' means coming soon; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: The offing is the stretch of sea visible near the horizon, so in the offing means coming soon.

clue.text: Shoot from China to America?

definitions.meaning: a young shoot is a new growth on a plant
china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), and an American word for a mate is buddy, shortened

explanation.surface: A plant's new growth exported from China to the US.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A bud is a young shoot on a plant, and bud is also American slang for a pal or friend.

clue.text: Rake Bob's gone cavorting with a female

indicators.note: cavorting is leaping about wildly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A rake, a womanising cad, has run off with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' looks like a libertine, which suits the cavorting, but here it means a very thin person.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a very thin person, and a bag of bones describes someone extremely skinny.

clue.text: Time to give women with children to support the vote

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece supports another by sitting below it

parts.note: X is the mark made on a ballot paper
mas are mothers, women with children

explanation.surface: Mothers are given time off to back the ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue MAS sits below X, supporting it.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is the season of giving presents, and Xmas is its short written form.

clue.text: You learn broken, halting English here — not the Queen's

indicators.note: broken letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A language school where you learn broken, faltering English, not the proper kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Halting' says the E of 'English' stops being part of the letters: YOU LEARN less E gives the seven letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Unroyal means not belonging to royalty, so something that is not the monarch's own.

clue.text: Metal badge: one breaks one off the wall

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: one piece breaking another splits it open and sits inside

parts.note: rum is old slang for odd or eccentric, like off the wall
an ID badge identifies its wearer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A metal badge splits apart as it falls off a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: ID followed by I breaks into I plus RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridium is a hard, dense, silvery-white metallic element of the platinum group.

clue.text: A bad lot on the far right tried to do harm

indicators.note: the letter at the far right of each word is its last one

explanation.surface: Someone describes a nasty gang from the extreme right who tried to cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the far right' looks political but picks the last letters of the four words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom is a grim fate, and one's lot in life is one's fate.

clue.text: Woman making up the numbers, as no good with pressure

parts.note: so can mean as, as in 'so far' and 'as far'
stress is mental or physical pressure

explanation.surface: A woman added just to make up the numbers is said to be useless under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making up the numbers' sounds like filling a team, but numbers are songs, and she composes them.
explanation.definitionFit: A songstress is a female singer, and in this cryptic sense one who makes up songs, called numbers.
